integrations.totpHelp: After enabling, the login will ask for a code from an authenticator app in addition to your password.
integrations.totpQrHelp: Open your authenticator app (Google/Microsoft Authy, etc.), add a new account and scan the code, or type the secret manually if scanning is not possible.

integrations.panelTokensHelp: For scripts, CI or tools without a browser: send the token in the HTTP header “Authorization: Bearer”. You decide which zones it applies to, whether it is read-only and when it expires – it can never do more than your own account.
integrations.apiInfoTitle: What is the API, where is it documented?
integrations.apiInfoP1: The web UI talks to a REST API under the path {{prefix}} on the same host as the app (e.g. https://your-server:5380).
integrations.apiInfoP2: A panel token is just another way to sign in to the same API: instead of a session cookie you send “Authorization: Bearer <complete token>”. Settings, user administration and credentials (password, 2FA, passkeys, tokens, webhooks) always require a browser login.
integrations.apiInfoP3: A written overview (curl example, token types) is in the repository file docs/PANEL-API.md. If the admin enables it, interactive OpenAPI is available at /docs (DOCS_ENABLED in the server environment).

integrations.passkeysHelp: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or a security key – no password required. Passkeys are bound to this domain and stay on your device.
integrations.passkeyInfoBody: A passkey is a cryptographic key pair. The private key never leaves your device (phone, laptop, security key); the server only stores the public key. It is phishing-resistant and cannot be reused across sites. You can register several (e.g. laptop + phone).

zoneDetail.hintSOA:
Order (space-separated): Primary NS · RNAME (SOA email as hostmaster.example.com.) · Serial · Refresh · Retry · Expire · Minimum.
Example: ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 2025010101 3600 900 1209600 3600
zoneDetail.hintNS:
Nameserver hostname as FQDN (trailing dot recommended).
Example: ns1.provider.net.
zoneDetail.hintA:
IPv4 address only, no port.
Example: 93.184.216.34
zoneDetail.hintALIAS:
Single target hostname (flat alias, provider-specific).
Example: target.example.com.
zoneDetail.hintMX:
Priority (lower = higher preference) and mail server FQDN.
Example: priority 10, server mail.example.com.
zoneDetail.hintTXT:
Any text. SPF/DKIM/DMARC often use TXT.
Example: v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com ~all
zoneDetail.hintSPF:
Same as TXT content (legacy RR type; TXT is preferred for new SPF).
Example: v=spf1 a mx ~all
zoneDetail.hintSRV:
priority · weight · port · target (FQDN).
Example: 10 5 443 sip.example.com.
zoneDetail.hintHTTPS:
RFC 9460: priority, target, SvcParams (e.g. alpn, port).
Example: 0 pool.example.net. alpn=h2
zoneDetail.hintSVCB:
Same family as HTTPS RR: priority, target, optional params.
Example: 0 pool.example.net. port=443
zoneDetail.hintCAA:
flag, tag, quoted value or ";" for issuewild.
Example: 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
zoneDetail.hintPTR:
Hostname for reverse zone.
Example: mail.example.com.
zoneDetail.hintTLSA:
usage · selector · matching-type · certificate hash (hex).
Example: 3 1 1 a9b8…
zoneDetail.hintLOC:
RFC 1876 format (lat/long/alt).
Short example: 52 22 23.000 N 4 53 32.000 E 10m
zoneDetail.hintNAPTR:
order · preference · flags · service · regexp · replacement
Example: 100 10 "S" "SIP+D2U" "!^.*$!sip:…" _sip._udp.example.com.
zoneDetail.hintDS:
KeyTag · Algorithm · DigestType · Digest(hex).
Example: 12345 8 2 abcd…
zoneDetail.hintDNSKEY:
Flags · Protocol · Algorithm · public key (Base64).
Example: 256 3 8 AwEAA…
zoneDetail.hintNSEC:
Next owner name · type list (NSEC bitmap).
Example: next.example.com. A AAAA RRSIG NSEC
zoneDetail.hintNSEC3:
Algorithm · Flags · Iterations · Salt · Hash · Next hash · types.
Usually copied from your DNSSEC tooling.
zoneDetail.hintNSEC3PARAM:
Algorithm · Flags · Iterations · Salt(hex).
Required for NSEC3 chains.
zoneDetail.hintRRSIG:
Type · Algorithm · Labels · OrigTTL · Expire · Inception · KeyTag · Signer · Signature(Base64).
Usually generated by DNSSEC tools.
zoneDetail.hintOPENPGPKEY:
OpenPGP packet in Base64 (RFC 7929).
Export with gpg --export etc.

webhooks.help: Your own HTTPS endpoint receives a signed JSON message when records, zones, DNSSEC or DynDNS change – with retries and a delivery log.
webhooks.infoBody: The server sends a POST with a JSON body. Verify it with the shared secret: compute HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body and compare it with the value after sha256= in the X-DNS-Manager-Signature header. Failed deliveries are retried up to 6 times; the X-DNS-Manager-Delivery header stays the same – use it to detect duplicates.

propagation.title: Propagation check
propagation.intro: Compares this zone's SOA serial across all panel servers, the authoritative name servers and public resolvers.
propagation.compareContent: Compare zone content between panel servers
propagation.compareContentHint: Loads the full zone from every panel server – slower for large zones.
propagation.summaryInSync: All {{total}} sources are up to date.
propagation.summaryPartial: {{ok}} of {{total}} sources up to date, {{mismatch}} differ, {{failed}} failed.
propagation.timedOut: The overall limit of 8 seconds was reached – unanswered queries are marked as timed out.
propagation.externalDisabled: External DNS queries are disabled – only the panel servers are compared via the PowerDNS API.
propagation.noNameservers: The zone has no NS records at the apex – authoritative check skipped.
propagation.singleServer: Only one panel server is configured – no server comparison possible.
propagation.separateBackendsInfo: The zone lives on several writable panel servers with separate databases: different serials are normal there, the zone content is compared instead.
propagation.whySeparateBackends: Panel servers with separate databases increase their serials independently – different serials are normal then. What matters is the content ("Compare zone content").
propagation.whySharedBackend: Servers sharing one database always show the same serial.
propagation.whySoaEdit: The serial shown is the one served (after SOA-EDIT); it may differ from the stored serial.
propagation.whySecondaries: Secondaries pick up changes only after NOTIFY and a zone transfer (AXFR/IXFR).
propagation.whyResolverCache: Public resolvers serve their cached answer until the TTL expires.
propagation.whyIpv6: IPv6 targets are only queried when IPv6 is enabled in the settings (Docker networks often lack IPv6).
propagation.note_separate_backend: Separate database – the content is compared, not the serial.
propagation.note_content_same_serial_differs: Content identical, only the serial differs.
propagation.note_resolver_cache: Resolver cache: up to {{ttl}} s left
propagation.note_secondary_lagging: Secondary has not picked up the new serial yet.
propagation.note_lua_not_comparable: LUA/ALIAS record – the answer is computed dynamically, no comparison.
propagation.note_truncated_targets: Only the first 12 name server addresses are queried.
propagation.note_ns_from_glue: Address taken from the zone data

propagation.err_not_loaded: Server not loaded (API key missing or unreadable)
propagation.err_refused: Query refused (REFUSED) – server is not responsible for the zone
propagation.err_not_authoritative: Answer not authoritative – possibly a lame delegation

bulk.syntaxHelpBody: One line per value: name [TTL] [IN] type content. Names without a trailing dot are relative to the zone, @ is the zone itself. $ORIGIN and $TTL are allowed, comments start with ;. Disabled values start with ;@disabled. TXT strings may be at most 255 characters (split longer ones into several "…" "…"). SOA and DNSSEC records (RRSIG, NSEC, NSEC3) are not allowed.

hint.activeUnpublished: At least one active key is not published. That is only normal during an algorithm rollover.
hint.algorithmRollover: Keys with different algorithms exist (algorithm rollover). Finish it via the key table.
hint.apiRectifyOff: API-RECTIFY is off for this zone. After changes via the API the NSEC/NSEC3 chain can become stale. Save the NSEC settings once to switch it on.
hint.deprecatedAlgorithm: Algorithm {{algorithm}} is deprecated (RFC 8624). Plan a switch to ECDSAP256SHA256.
hint.keysInactiveOnly: Keys exist but none is active – the zone is not signed. Activate a key, or delete the keys and set up DNSSEC again.
hint.multipleActiveSep: Several KSK/CSK are active – normal during a rollover. The registrar should then list the DS of both keys.
hint.noActiveSep: No active KSK/CSK: the DS at the registrar cannot point to a signing key. Validating resolvers return SERVFAIL once a DS is registered.
hint.nsec3IterationsHigh: NSEC3 uses {{iterations}} iterations – many resolvers treat that as insecure. Please lower it to 0.
hint.nsec3IterationsNonzero: NSEC3 uses {{iterations}} additional iteration(s). RFC 9276 recommends 0.
hint.nsec3Salt: NSEC3 uses a salt. RFC 9276 recommends not using a salt.
hint.peersDivergent: On {{servers}} this zone has different DNSSEC keys. Separate databases with different keys cause validation failures – the keys must be synchronised manually (see docs). Right after a change, shared databases may show this briefly.
hint.peersUnreachable: These servers could not be checked: {{servers}}.
hint.peersUnsigned: On {{servers}} this zone is not signed. Once the DS is registered, answers from these servers fail validation.
hint.presignedZone: Presigned zone: signatures come from the primary, keys are not managed here.
hint.publishedUnsupported: PowerDNS {{version}} does not support the “published” flag (4.3 or later needed). Inactive keys are always published there; publish/unpublish is disabled.
hint.rolloverInProgress: A key rollover is in progress ({{phase}}). Open the rollover assistant to continue.
hint.secondariesSerial: Master zone: secondaries that transfer the signed zone via AXFR only pick up new keys after a serial increase. The panel increases the serial after key changes and sends a NOTIFY (can be switched off in the dialogs).
hint.secondaryZoneSigning: Secondary zone with its own keys: PowerDNS signs the data received via AXFR itself (front-signing). The primary must deliver unsigned data for that.
hint.serverReadOnly: Server “{{server}}” is set to “Save: No” – DNSSEC changes are blocked here.
hint.sha1Ds: You should no longer use DS lines with digest type 1 (SHA-1) at your registrar.
hint.versionUnknown: The PowerDNS version is unknown – version-dependent functions are offered without a pre-check.

dnssec.rolloverKindSep: Roll the KSK/CSK (with DS change at the registrar)
dnssec.rolloverNoActive: There is no active key of this kind. Activate a key first.
dnssec.rolloverRetireBody: The old key (tag {{oldTag}}) no longer signs but stays published so cached signatures remain valid.
dnssec.rolloverSinceUnknown: time unknown (not done via the panel)
